request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Information: 
Name: [REDACTED]
DOB: [REDACTED]
Gender: Male
Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 48-year-old male with a history of poorly controlled type 1 diabetes mellitus, presented with a neuroischemic ulcer of the fifth toe, which was classified as a grade 3 infection. He was diagnosed with signs of osteomyelitis and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

Treatment: 
The patient was treated with oral vancomycin and underwent wound care management according to the TIME algorithm for 1.5 months. The wound bed was cleaned and decontaminated, devitalized tissue was debrided, non-irritant skin protector was applied to protect the peri-lesional tissue, hydrogel was applied to the wound bed, nanocrystalline silver dressing was used, and polyurethane foam dressing was applied. After full healing, the patient's pre-prandial glucose and HbA1c levels improved.

Discharge Information: 
The patient was discharged with no acute complaints. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled with his primary care physician and podiatrist. A detailed instruction sheet for wound care management and glycemic control was provided to the patient.

Condition at Discharge: 
Stable with no acute complaints. Condition improved.

Instructions: 
1. Follow up with Primary Care Physician and Podiatrist.
2. Follow wound care instructions.
3. Maintain healthy diet and exercise regime.
4. Monitor blood sugar levels.
5. Attend scheduled appointments.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
In ICD-10-AM, diabetic foot ulcer with infection and osteomyelitis in a type 1 diabetic is coded to E10.- (type 1 diabetes mellitus), using the .5 subdivision for peripheral circulatory complications (neuroischemic ulcer) or .7 for multiple complications in Australian coding. The osteomyelitis (M86) and the MRSA (B95.62) would be additional codes.

The principal diagnosis is therefore the diabetes category, E10. The neuroischemic ulcer is a diabetic complication, and the chief reason for care was treating the diabetic foot ulcer and infection.

Under ICD-10-AM, E10.73 is "with foot ulcer due to multiple causes", and the 3-character category is E10.

CODE: E10
